newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary Committee not discussing punt-source.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary Committee not discussing punt-source.

text.p: The EU Monetary Committee is not discussing the question of the Irish punt at its meeting today, a committee source said.
Asked whether there had been discussions about the punt, which has risen to close to its 15 percent fluctuation limit within the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism, the source said: "No, No".
The source was speaking as the committee broke up for lunch. The meeting was to continue this afternoon.

The committee of national treasury and central bank officials was meeting amid rife market speculation of a possible revaluation of the punt, but officials have said it will focus on a number of issues pertaining to economic and monetary union, in particular future relations between EU finance ministers and a European Central Bank.

EU monetary officials on Wednesday said the Irish economy's fundamentals did not justify a revaluation of the punt. "There is no intention whatsoever to talk about the Irish punt," a senior EU official told Reuters.

The meeting was also to discuss the relationship between the euro and currencies such as dollar, as well as the impact EMU will have on the International Monetary Fund. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
